claim: A change that moves a page type leaves that page type resolving nowhere in the world the change makes. Over a change taking akasha/text-property.page-type.ts away and writing akasha/types/text-property.page-type.ts, `listedAt(root, "page-type", "text-property")` answers an empty list where it answered the new path before. tests-pass carries a test named for exactly this, and that test has failed 11 of the 12 newest audit rounds, having failed none of the 12 before them. It is no race: the assertion answers a refusal rather than timing out, and the refusal carries the inner run's own output naming the empty list. Anything judging a change that moves a page type reads the index as though the type were gone, so a landing that moves one is judged against a world where nothing of that type resolves.

evidence:
Read on 2026-09-21 against this checkout.

What the test does. `a run under a change that moves a page type resolves that page type where it lands`, in check/code/pages/tests-pass/tests-pass.check-code.decision.test.ts, builds a scratch repository, makes a landing that takes TYPE_WAS away and writes TYPE_NOW with the same body, adds akasha/one.module.test.ts carrying RESOLVES, and asks `refusalsOver` for the refusals over that landing. It expects none.

What it answers now. One refusal, against akasha/one.module.test.ts, carrying the inner run's output: `const found = listedAt(process.cwd(), "page-type", "text-property")` then `expect(found.map((one) => one.path)).toEqual(["akasha/types/text-property.page-type.ts"])`, received `[]`. So the inner test ran, reached the index, and the index named no page of that type at the path the change writes it to.

How it was read. A measuring apply answers only what a file spent, so it says `did not come back clean` and no more. An apply carrying the file answers the refusal whole, which is where the inner output above comes from. The verdict rows beside tests-pass truncate the refusal, so the inner output cannot be read back out of the log.

When it started. Over the twelve audit rounds before the newest twelve, tests-pass named email-rule-reading, program-naming, lualib-builder, name-session, binary-running, cut-fingerprint, day-opening, running.module, block-akasha-edits and render-harness-run, and did not name this file once. Over the newest twelve it named it eleven times. So this began between those windows rather than having always been so.

Where the answer comes from. `listedAt` in page/index/modules/reading/index-reading.module.code.ts hands its arguments to `listedNamed`, which derives an index path through `filedAt` and reads it with `listedIn(readingIn(given))`. For this lookup that path is the one filed under page-type, page-type, slug and text-property. The inner test hands it `process.cwd()`, which is the merged world the change makes, so the entry for the moved page type has to have been written into that world by the settle the change makes of its own. An empty answer says that entry is not there, rather than that the reading is wrong.

What is unmeasured. No commit has been shown to be the step. page/index/modules/settling was narrowed to the change's own files earlier the same day, and page-composing was changed to take a page type's pages under `pages` where its folder is named that type's plural, both of which touch where a page of a type is looked for, but neither has been run against this test to see it turn.
